# Self Dividing Numbers.

@example 132, 135, 144 and 155 are multiples of each of their digits; 130, 140, 150 and 160 contain a 0, and every other number fails on some digit.
130
160
=> [132,135,144,155]

@example 16 to 19 and 21 each have a digit that leaves a remainder, and 20 contains a 0.
16
21
=> []

@example The single digits divide themselves, 10 contains a 0, and 11 and 12 pass.
7
12
=> [7,8,9,11,12]

# The smallest range.
1
1
=> [1]

# A 0 as the last digit rules the number out; it isn't skipped, and it
# must not be divided by.
10
10
=> []

20
20
=> []

# A 0 in the middle rules a number out too: 101 to 109 all have one.
101
109
=> []

# Each digit must divide the whole number, not what is left of it after
# the digits to its right are dropped: 21 is not a multiple of 2, nor 25
# of 2.
21
25
=> [22,24]

# The range starts far from 1, and its first number qualifies.
36
40
=> [36]

# Repeated digits.
2222
2224
=> [2222,2224]

# The only answer is above 255.
255
270
=> [264]

# The top of the range: 10000 has zeros, and 9999 is the largest
# self-dividing number allowed.
9900
9999
=> [9936,9999]

9999
10000
=> [9999]

10000
10000
=> []

# The longest stretch with no self-dividing number at all: 5775 and 6126
# are self-dividing, and nothing between them is.
5776
6125
=> []

# 128 answers, the last at the right end of the range.
300
2848
